question: What percentage of tests will be positive for seasonal human coronaviruses (all types) in the United States for the week ending October 24, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for seasonal human coronaviruses (all types) in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-24 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
# US seasonal coronavirus test positivity (CDC NREVSS), week ending 2026-10-24: research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on CDC dataset rgnm-fkqb, using the national row for pathogen "HCOV", subtype "Combined Type". [data.cdc.gov API](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Each weekly posting replaces the whole dataset, so only one version is online at a time. I could not open an archived early-October copy because archive.org is blocked for my fetch tool. The numbers below come from the current online version, and I used only weeks up to 2026-09-26, which is roughly what was public by 2026-10-05. Earlier weeks can be revised slightly after first posting.
- Most recent week available as of about 2026-10-02 (week ending 2026-09-26): 0.68% (133 positives out of 19,649 tests). [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The target week starts 2026-10-18.
- The national level has been flat at about 0.5 to 0.7% since mid-June. It edged up through September as testing volume grew.

## 3. Recent news
- I found no news or CDC commentary specific to the seasonal (non-COVID) coronaviruses in 2026. The search turned up only background material.
- Background: in the six HCoV seasons before the pandemic, the season started in October or November and peaked in January or February. [PMC8689701](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8689701/)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
Recent national weekly values for 2026, as shown in the current dataset version:
- 2026-09-26: 0.68 (19,649 tests)
- 2026-09-19: 0.65
- 2026-09-12: 0.54
- 2026-09-05: 0.63
- 2026-08-29: 0.67
- 2026-08-22: 0.59
- 2026-08-15: 0.50
- 2026-08-08: 0.66
- 2026-08-01: 0.44
- 2026-07-04: 0.76
- 2026-06-06: 0.92
- 2026-05-23: 1.31 (tail end of the spring decline)

[data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

Week-to-week noise is typically about ±0.05 to 0.15 percentage points.

Same calendar window in past years, from the end of September to the week ending around October 24:

| Year | Late Sep | ~Oct 24 week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 0.39 (9/28) | 0.47 (10/19), 0.62 (10/26) | +0.08 to +0.23 |
| 2020 | 0.16 (9/26) | 0.21 (10/24) | +0.05 (pandemic disruption) |
| 2021 | 0.73 (9/25) | 0.58 (10/23) | -0.15 |
| 2022 | 0.28 (9/24) | 0.42 (10/22) | +0.14 |
| 2023 | 0.52 (9/23), 0.41 (9/30) | 0.44 (10/21) | -0.08 / +0.03 |
| 2024 | 0.75 (9/28) | 1.14 (10/19), 1.53 (10/26) | +0.39 to +0.78 |
| 2025 | 0.27 (9/27) | 0.33 (10/25) | +0.06 |

- Over this four-week window the change ranged from -0.15 to +0.78 points. The median is about +0.06 to +0.14. In most years the main rise starts in early or mid November. 2024 was the exception, with an early October takeoff.
- 2026 is running higher than 2022, 2023 and 2025, and about the same as 2021 and 2024 at this point. This year's summer floor (about 0.5 to 0.7%) is well above 2025's (about 0.3%).
- Simply carrying the 2026-09-26 value forward with the historical changes gives roughly 0.53 to 1.46%, with the middle of the range around 0.7 to 0.8%. The question's range tops out at 1.5.

[data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I did not find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets, or any expert forecasts, on HCoV percent positivity. I did not run a separate prediction-market search, so a market could exist that I missed.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly CDC postings due around 2026-10-09, 10-16 and 10-23 will cover the weeks ending 10/3, 10/10 and 10/17. The resolving posting is due 2026-10-30.
- Schools are back in session and testing volume is rising, about 19.6k tests a week compared with 14k in July. Seasonal onset usually comes in October or November. [PMC8689701](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8689701/)
- Weather is only an indirect factor. I did not pull a seasonal outlook.

Sources: [data.cdc.gov rgnm-fkqb](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json), [PMC8689701](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8689701/), [catalog.data.gov](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/percent-of-tests-positive-for-viral-respiratory-pathogens), [EID 31/8](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/31/8/25-0451-f1)
